rationale: Target: tool/line mismatches in the round-1 (current best, 0.7194) failures, which hit speak_and_act (0.75 = 27/36) and action_correct together. (1) S11 x3: the agent correctly says rung 3 'I'm unable to assist at this time. Goodbye' but calls respond, so the call never hangs up. A rule that any goodbye means end_call fixes all three. (2) Transfer turns: S25#r3 says the transfer line but calls respond (labelled transfer). S15#r2/r3, S17#r2/r3 and S20 x3 say 'Great, thank you for confirming that.' via respond while the gate is unmet, and every transfer-bucket reply_quality judgement fails (0.00). Making the transfer line legal only inside transfer_call, with an explicit fallback to 'ask for the missing one' when the gate is unmet, should turn those into on-script follow-up questions instead of premature transfers. The existing TRANSFER PRECONDITION and what_counts_as_an_answer rules still decide whether the gate is met. (3) S29 x3 (voicemail 'please record your message... press pound'): the agent uses the ladder rung 3 or the no-response line, but the label accepts only the voicemail or IVR closing. The script's voicemail line ('I'll try again later, goodbye') is restated here because ending_the_call lists automated audio under the not-engaging ladder, which conflicts. Predicted: speak_and_act from 0.75 to about 0.86-0.94 (S11 +3, S29 +2-3, S25 +1); action_correct +0.03-0.04; transfer reply_quality up from 0 on 3-6 of its rows. Risk: some S17/S20 rows could flip to a premature transfer_call instead of a question. The fallback wording is there to prevent that. Gate safety is watched. About +170 prompt tokens (~1.5%), so first-action p50 should stay near 640-660ms, under 700ms. Weighted quality should rise about +0.04 to +0.07.
